label: early original step (t=3-5) after d/k, in sequences starting with e/v/x/u/w
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). It fires almost only at steps 3-5 of the original phase, plus a little at the delimiter / first copy step of short sequences. It fires on a specific prefix: one or two steps after a d or k (prev_tok d/k has about 12x lift), most strongly when the sequence starts with e/v/x/u/w and orig(1) is u/e/v. Top examples look like e u d k [g], v u k k [q], v e d k [3]. Magnitude is highest for these canonical prefixes (e.g. e u d k at t=4). It does not fire at t<3, it is nearly silent in the copy phase, and the current token matters little. The predicate recovers about 70% of activation mass but has only ~3% precision, so the prefix pattern is necessary but far from sufficient. The feature looks like a rare conjunction of several early tokens (a hidden-state direction) that simple predicates do not isolate.
